strategy.summary: Two tests on main fail. formatPrice now returns '12.50 USD' instead of '$12.50', a deliberate change recorded in CHANGELOG 1.1.0, so test/money.test.js is stale and gets updated (plus a case for the new currency argument). shippingFor(5000) returns 499 because the RATES band check uses `subtotal > over`, which contradicts FREE_SHIPPING_FROM ("this much or more ships free"). That is an application defect: the assertion stays, a defect is recorded, and the test is marked expected-to-fail.
outOfScope: Changing application source (src/shipping.js fix belongs to the dev team)
assumptions: CHANGELOG 1.1.0 states the formatPrice change ('12.50 USD', currency as second argument) is intended, so the old '$12.50' expectation is a test bug.
Goods costing exactly $50.00 should ship free, as the FREE_SHIPPING_FROM doc comment and the existing test say (asked as Q1). The RATES `>` check is therefore the defect.
openQuestions: Q1: should exactly $50.00 ship free (FREE_SHIPPING_FROM doc) or only above $50 (RATES doc 'applies above its over')?

defects.title: shippingFor charges $4.99 on goods costing exactly $50 (FREE_SHIPPING_FROM)
defects.description: AC3: FREE_SHIPPING_FROM (5000) is documented as "orders whose goods cost this much or more ship free", and the test from the last good run expected shippingFor(5000) === 0. But shippingFor picks its band from RATES with `subtotal > b.over` (src/shipping.js:18). The free band { over: 5000 } therefore applies only above 5000, and exactly 5000 gets the flat 499. orderTotal inherits this. Fix: compare with `>=` for non-zero bands, or derive the free band from FREE_SHIPPING_FROM.
defects.evidence: AssertionError: expected 499 to be +0 at test/shipping.test.js:11 (shippingFor(FREE_SHIPPING_FROM))

questions.question: Should an order whose goods cost exactly $50.00 ship free? The constant FREE_SHIPPING_FROM in src/shipping.js says orders costing "this much or more" ship free, and the existing test agrees. But the RATES table that shippingFor actually uses applies a band only strictly above its `over` value, so at exactly 5000 cents it charges $4.99.
questions.assumption: Yes, exactly $50 ships free. I'll keep the shippingFor(5000) === 0 assertion, record the `>`-vs-`>=` boundary as an application defect, and mark that test expected-to-fail. The formatPrice failure is a test bug, because CHANGELOG 1.1.0 deliberately changed the format to '12.50 USD', so I'll update that test.
questions.answer: No preference from the reviewer: decide yourself from the code, record the decision as an assumption and carry on.
